title: Fantasia, 1940 — the first commercial film in stereo, and a flop

post.facebook:
On this day in 1940, Walt Disney's Fantasia premiered at the Broadway Theatre in New York — the first commercial film shown with stereophonic sound.

Disney wanted audiences to feel "as though they were standing at the podium" with the conductor, Leopold Stokowski. Thirty-three microphones surrounded the Philadelphia Orchestra, feeding eight recording machines. In the theatre, a new system called Fantasound moved the music between speakers; installing it took a week, around the clock. It was the same theatre where Mickey Mouse's Steamboat Willie had played 12 years earlier.

More than 1,000 artists drew over 500 characters, and Mickey got pupils in his eyes for the first time. But one Fantasound setup cost $85,000, the distributor RKO called it a "longhair musical", and despite rave reviews the film was a box-office failure at first.

Today it is counted among the greatest animated films ever made, and it was chosen for the U.S. National Film Registry in 1990.

Also on 13 November: the Holland Tunnel opened under the Hudson (1927), and a total solar eclipse darkened northern Australia (2012).
